cards.text: Here in the book of Jeremiah comes a word from the LORD for the house of Israel. Just before this, the LORD said His people had gone after the Baals (Jeremiah 9:14). So grab a seat, friend, because today the LORD is talking about the gods people make for themselves.
The LORD starts here: do not learn the ways of the nations. Then He brings up the signs in the heavens, the ones the nations look up at and get TERRIFIED by.

cards.question: The LORD tells Israel to be terrified by the signs in the heavens.

cards.text: Then the LORD calls the customs of the peoples worthless. And He walks through how one of their gods gets made, step by step, like a recipe card.

cards.question: Step one in making one of these gods. Where does it start out?

answers.text: A tree cut down from the forest
A stone dug up from the riverbed
A lump of clay from the potter

cards.text: A craftsman shapes it with a chisel, and then they adorn it with silver and gold. Friend, that is a VERY expensive piece of firewood.

cards.question: Next, they fasten the silver and gold idol with hammer and nails. Why?

answers.text: So it faces the right way

cards.text: If your god needs NAILS to keep from tipping over, friend, you didn't get a god, you got furniture. Then the LORD gives a picture: their idols are like scarecrows in a cucumber patch.

cards.question: Like scarecrows, these idols cannot speak. And since they cannot walk, they must be ___.
The LORD tells Israel not to fear these idols. Why not?

answers.text: They can do no harm and no good
They are too far away to hurt anyone
The LORD has already broken them

cards.text: Then the passage turns and speaks right to the LORD: "There is none like You, O LORD." It says the LORD is great, and His name is mighty in power.

cards.question: The passage asks, "Who would not fear You, O King of nations?" Among all the wise men of the nations, how many are like the LORD?

cards.text: Then it says, "But they are altogether senseless and foolish, instructed by worthless idols made of wood!" Friend, that's like taking baking lessons from an empty cookie box.
Then the passage goes right back to how idols get made. Gold is brought from Uphaz, and the idols are the work of a craftsman from the hands of a goldsmith.

cards.question: The idols' gold comes from Uphaz, and their hammered silver is brought from ___.
Last, the idols get dressed in blue and purple. Who fashions those clothes?

cards.text: After all that silver, gold and fancy clothes, here comes the turn, friend. The passage says the LORD is the true God.

cards.question: But the LORD is the true God; He is the ___ God and eternal King.

cards.text: And this King is not sitting on a shelf waiting to be dusted. The earth quakes at His wrath, and the nations cannot endure His indignation.

cards.question: Next come words to pass on about these idol gods. What do the words say will happen to them?

answers.text: They will perish from this earth
They will be locked away in a temple
They will be melted down into coins

cards.text: And the words point out that these gods made neither the heavens nor the earth. Friend, they couldn't make it across the ROOM without somebody carrying them.
Now compare that with the LORD. He made the earth by His power, established the world by His wisdom and stretched out the heavens by His understanding.

cards.question: Then the passage turns to thunder and rain. When the LORD thunders, what roars?

cards.text: The LORD makes the clouds rise from the ends of the earth, sends lightning with the rain and brings the wind out of His storehouses. Then the passage says every man is senseless and devoid of knowledge.

cards.question: The passage says every goldsmith is proud of his idols.
The goldsmith's molten images are a ___, and there is no breath in them.

cards.text: The LORD runs thunder, lightning and wind, and these idols can't even fog up a mirror. The passage calls them worthless, a work to be mocked, and says they will perish in the time of their punishment.

cards.question: Last, the passage calls the LORD the Portion of Jacob. Jacob is the father of Israel's twelve tribes (Genesis 49:28). Why is the Portion of Jacob not like these idols?

answers.text: He is the Maker of all things

cards.question: The passage says Israel is the tribe of the LORD's inheritance.

cards.text: The passage closes with this: the LORD of Hosts is His name. Those idols needed a craftsman, a goldsmith and a box of nails just to stand up straight, but the LORD made the craftsman, the gold AND the whole forest.
